title: Rosa's busy week
scenario:
Rosa uses a chat app and a browser helper (an AI app that can read web pages and click for them) for everyday jobs. This week four things happen:

1. Rosa's bank charged a fee twice, and Rosa wants help with a complaint letter.
2. Rosa asks the browser helper to collect three soup recipes from cooking sites.
3. Rosa wants to show a friend a long chat about Rosa's own health.
4. A video of the town's mayor saying "the tap water is unsafe" spreads in a neighbours' group.

Rosa asks you what to do each time.

questions.prompt: For the complaint letter, Rosa is about to paste the full bank statement, with the account and card numbers. What is the safe way?

options.text: Paste the full statement, because the app needs every detail to write a good letter.
options.explanation: The letter only needs the problem: a fee charged twice, the date and the amount. The Claude Help Center asks you to be thoughtful about sharing credit card numbers and bank account details.

options.text: Describe the double fee, its date and amount, and leave the account and card numbers out.
options.explanation: Right. The app can write the letter from the facts of the problem. Rosa adds the account number to the final letter, outside the chat. The Gemini Apps Help says not to enter confidential data you wouldn't want a reviewer to see.

options.text: Paste it, then delete the chat at once, so nobody can ever see what was in it.
options.explanation: Deleting may not remove every copy. The Gemini help says chats picked for human review are kept for up to three years even after you delete your activity. Safer to leave the numbers out.

options.text: Paste only a photo of the statement, because apps can't read numbers in a picture.
options.explanation: A photo still shows the same account and card numbers. Leaving them out is the safe way.

questions.prompt: While collecting recipes, the browser helper suddenly opens Rosa's email and starts a message to an address Rosa doesn't know. What should Rosa do?

options.text: Let it finish, because the helper probably has a good reason for the email.
options.explanation: Rosa asked for recipes, not an email. A web page may have hidden instructions that took over the task. This is prompt injection.

options.text: Wait to see what the message says, then decide whether to let it be sent.
options.explanation: Waiting gives a possible attack more time, and the message may hold Rosa's private data. Stop first, look later.

options.text: Ask the helper why it opened the email, and go on if the reason sounds fine.
options.explanation: If hidden instructions took over the helper, its explanation can't be trusted. Stop the task first.

options.text: Stop the task at once, because a page may have hidden instructions, then report it.
options.explanation: Right. The Claude Help Center says that if the helper starts visiting unexpected sites or asking for sensitive information, you should stop the task immediately, because it could be prompt injection.

questions.prompt: Rosa wants to send the health chat to one friend as a public share link. What should Rosa know first?

options.text: Anyone who gets the link can open it, and the friend could forward it or post it.
options.explanation: Right. The Claude Help Center says to treat a public link as public: anyone with it can view the chat, with no account, and there is no way to limit it to one person.

options.text: A link sent to one person is private, so only that friend can ever open it.
options.explanation: The Claude Help Center says a link sent to one person is still public. Whoever has it can forward or post it.

options.text: If Rosa turns the link off later, every copy anyone made is deleted too.
options.explanation: Turning the link off stops the link. The Claude Help Center says it can't remove copies or screenshots someone already made.

options.text: Public links are hidden from search engines, so nobody else can ever find it.
options.explanation: The Claude Help Center says Anthropic asks search engines not to list it, but can't control where the link is posted or who copies it.

questions.prompt: Rosa checks the mayor video with an AI checker. It says: "no AI watermark found". What does that tell Rosa?

options.text: The video is real, because the checker would surely find a mark if AI had made it.
options.explanation: The Gemini Apps Help says a missing SynthID mark means Google AI didn't make it, but other AI systems could have. The Claude Help Center says a missing mark doesn't prove the content wasn't AI-made.

options.text: Little: another AI tool could have made it, so Rosa checks the town's own channels.
options.explanation: Right. A missing mark is not proof. Rosa looks for the message on the town's official website or channels before sharing or believing it.

options.text: The video is fake, because a real video of a mayor would always carry an official mark.
options.explanation: Real videos usually carry no AI mark at all. A missing mark proves nothing either way.

options.text: Rosa should share it right now with a note, since the check has already been done.
options.explanation: The check said very little. Sharing an unchecked warning about tap water can scare a whole street for nothing.
